title: The quant salary problem
prompt: Eight quants from different banks want to calculate their group's average salary. However, none of them is willing to reveal their individual salary to anyone else.
They have no trusted third party and no secure computer system. They can only pass numbers to each other.
What does the first quant add to their salary before passing the sum along?
hints: If quant 1 passes their exact salary to quant 2, everyone who sees the running total can work backwards to figure out salaries. How do you prevent that?
Quant 1 can disguise their salary by adding something only they know — something they can remove at the end.
The added value must be known only to quant 1, arbitrary in size, and removable once the full sum returns.
solution_lede:
The trick is for the first quant to add a secret random number — known only to them — before sharing anything.

Quant 1 picks a large random number R, adds their salary S₁, and passes R + S₁ to quant 2. Each subsequent quant simply adds their own salary and passes the total along. No one can infer any individual salary from the running total because R is unknown.

After quant 8 adds their salary and passes back to quant 1, the total is R + S₁ + S₂ + … + S₈. Quant 1 subtracts R to get the true total, then divides by 8. The average is revealed; no individual salary ever was.

solution_steps.body: Quant 1 chooses a large secret random number R, adds their salary S₁, and passes R + S₁ to quant 2.
Each of quants 2–8 adds their own salary to the running total and passes it on. No one knows R, so no salary is inferable.
Quant 8 passes the final total back to quant 1, who subtracts R to obtain S₁ + S₂ + … + S₈.
Quant 1 divides by 8 and announces the average. Individual salaries remain private.
